critiques.notes: Root رهن scoped cleanly; rahīn (52:21) and rahīnah (74:38) are both fa'īl carrying the maf'ūl sense — 'held-in-pledge,' not 'holding.' The buried gem the draft must surface: the gender concord — rahīn agrees with masculine imri', rahīnah with feminine nafs — the Quran matches the collateral's grammar to the debtor it names. Keep the pawnshop strictly illustrative; the theology is in kasaba/kasabat, not the analogy.

Lemma وَدُود correctly fenced off from the 29-verse root — that discipline is the whole survival of the piece. But 'the Most Loving' is a half-translation: wadūd is fa'ūl, and the classical lexicographers (al-Rāzī, al-Zajjāj) read the pattern as bearing both the active and the passive — He who loves and He who is loved. Naming only the active sense is a lexical loss, not an error. One of three near-identical Wadud submissions; only one ships.

The exclusivity law (طبع 11/11 with qalb, قسو 6/6) is real and morphologically clean, Form I throughout. The load-bearing caution is grammatical, not just theological: 9:87 and 63:3 are PASSIVE — the Quran withholds the agent precisely where the reader would supply 'God,' and that omission is itself the balāghah safety-valve against fatalism. If the draft flattens the two passives into the nine actives it misreads the text. Honor the kasb/istihqāʿ ikhtilāf and 74:31's disputed placement in the body. I want eyes on this before it ships.

Root برزخ scoped clean, 3 verses. Note lexically that barzakh is itself a naturalized loanword (Persian) meaning barrier/partition — the 'sea word' framing is the Quranic usage, not the etymon, and the draft should not imply the root is natively Arabic. 25:53 'adhb furāt / milh ujāj and 55:19-20 are accurate. Discipline required to keep the intermediate-state reading Quran-only and off the grave-punishment hadith material, and off the two-seas oceanography overreach.

khannās is fa''āl (habitual retreater), khunnas the plural of khānis — the star-link (81:15) is lexically sound and Hasan rightly caps the etymology. But 2:67 is glossed loosely: Musa seeks refuge 'an akūna min al-jāhilīn' — from BEING among the ignorant/frivolous, not narrowly 'from mockery.' Tighten that or the first-isti'ādhah hook overstates. Two threads (Musa's refuge + the khunnas name) welded to one payoff risks a seam; the second thread is the sharper reveal.

Exhibit is mis-cited — it lists GRAPH-9 (the zalzala verb), but the salām first/last bracket is BRACKET-9; the content is right, the reference is careless. The scope warning is the correct one and must be obeyed: lemma سَلام (n=42), because the سلم root drowns it in islām/muslim/sallama. 4:94 is combat-adjacent — the classical ruling (the prohibition is on refusing the greeting) must be visible so 'peace can be refused' does not read as license. 97:5 mercy reading is the standard one.

Root قمص, 6/6 inside Sūrat Yūsuf — clean, and she caught the pool's own correction (THREE same-surah roots: qamīṣ/ṣayd/kahf, not five). The lie-verdict-healing arc is textually anchored, not imposed. The comparative-Genesis move is the right instinct: give Joseph's coat its dignity and do NOT let the healing detail (12:93) be asserted as 'unique to the Quran' without qualification — that single word is where an outsider reader decides you are honest or triumphalist.

Lemma وَدُود, correctly fenced, comparative frame ('God is love') handled without strawman — good. Same fa'ūl note as its two siblings: the pattern carries loving-and-beloved, and dropping the passive sense is a lexical thinning. Mushaf-order bracket, not chronology — she states it. This is one of three Wadud pieces in the pool; on merit it is the most carefully framed, but freshness suffers because it competes with itself.

Same taba'/qasā/marad substrate as HASAN-3, scoped correctly (ROOT for the seal-counts, PHRASE for the marad bookends, 11 hits). Calls it an 'exclusivity law' — accurate. Slightly less guarded than Hasan on the two passive verses; the draft must still name that 9:87/63:3 suppress the agent. The kasb/earned-sealing ikhtilāf is flagged. Solid, but the sensitivity means it needs the same pre-ship read.

This is arithmetic, not balāghah, and the 'expected ~8' rests on an independence assumption that Quranic vocabulary flatly violates — roots cluster by discourse zone, so denial-language and forgiveness-language living in different verses is partly what thematic clustering already predicts, not a mystery. She discloses the assumption, which saves it from fatal, but 'statistically impossible-looking' overstates and a numerate skeptic will bite. The interpretive guardrail (the Quran DOES forgive former deniers; kadhaba the act ≠ the sealed state) is essential and correctly named.

Root قبس, naqtabis Form VIII (iqtibās, seeking-a-light-from) — accurate. But the freshness cost is heavy: /posts/musa-fire-three-tellings-quran already owns the word, the 'borrow a flame' framing, and two of the three occurrences. The genuinely new payload is a single verse (57:13, the wall). A whole article resting on one unshipped occurrence is thin; if it runs it must be explicitly a coda, not a re-tell.

Roots ضحك/بكي, both first at 9:82 ('fal-yaḍḥakū qalīlan wal-yabkū kathīran') — verified, and she flags mushaf-order-not-revelation, which is the honesty this genre lives or dies on. The best instinct in her set: the last laugh (83:34) is at the disbelievers' expense, and she refuses to soften it into a feel-good arc. That discomfort IS the accurate reading; keep it.

Root كظم, 6 verses, clean. The draft leaves morphology on the table: the root spreads across kāẓim (active participle, the one doing the swallowing), kaẓīm (fa'īl intensive, 12:84/16:58/43:17), and makẓūm (passive participle, 68:48 Yunus — the one swallowed/overwhelmed). That active-to-passive gradient IS the anatomy of held-in feeling and would give Khalil the transparency he wants. hanājir census (2 verses) is right. Frame around Ya'qub's grief as census, not as his story, to clear the published pieces.

نزغ 4/4 with Shayṭān is the strong verified core, and it is genuinely unshipped. But the khunnas/khannās half overlaps HASAN-5, which builds on the same GRAPH-1 — the panel cannot run both on that root. Minor lexical care: al-khannās in 114 is an epithet/description, not literally 'his name,' and the classical gloss is 'retreats when Allah is remembered' (Lane: khanasa = draw back) — the coward-who-jabs-and-hides reframe is fair on that basis.

Two tight complete-sets: karb 4/4 with najā, awjasa (Form IV, the concealed flicker) 3/3 answered by lā takhaf within a verse. Morphology accurate. The one guard that matters is named: three of the four karb verses are NARRATIVE rescues (Nūḥ, Mūsā), only 6:64 is general address — so 'the Quran welds rescue to distress' is a textual co-occurrence claim, NOT a worldly-rescue guarantee, and he says so. Differentiation from qunūt (tighter, no adjacency window) holds.

Third al-Wadūd in the pool, lemma-scoped (wadūd not the ḥabb root), both Meccan, no chronology claim — all correct. The 'both times paired with a mercy-name' observation is the freshest angle among the three Wadud framings. Same fa'ūl active/passive note. The 'sin freely' guard is real: the verses pair the name WITH a command to turn back (istighfār/tawbah); that pairing must stay intact. Only one Wadud piece can ship.

Bundles two brackets (ni'mah 1:7→102:8 and khulūd 2:25→104:3) into one article — that dilutes; each is a cleaner single reveal. The mandatory scope disclosure is correct and non-trivial: the نعم root folds in an'ām/livestock (33 of 140 tokens), so an undisclosed 'blessing appears 140 times' would be false. an'amta is Form IV, na'īm the noun — accurate. Mushaf-order flagged. Pick one bracket.

The strongest morphological backbone in the pool: yūqā is the passive of waqā — 'whoever is PROTECTED from the shuḥḥ of his soul' — and the passive voice IS the theology, repeated verbatim in 59:9/64:16. That is verifiable, counter-cultural, and skeptic-proof. Sharpen the lexis: shuḥḥ is the constitutional greed-plus-clinging, distinct from bukhl the act (Ibn Kathīr keeps them apart) — that distinction earns the 'factory setting' claim. 4:128 'uḥḍirat' = made-ever-present, so 'default' is fair, 'born greedy' is a shade strong. The shuḥḥ/ḥaḍḍ weld must read as one theme (inner grip / outward failure to feed), not two half-articles, and 'protection is received' must be held against the standing command to give so it never tips into fatalism.
